onion noun

classical

caepa, caepae f.

noun, first declension

Also spelled cēpa, with a neuter by-form caepe; the series’ spelling is caepa (Ep. VII). cf. Vulg. Num. 11, 5, where Israel remembers the cucumerēs, pepones, porrī and cēpae of Egypt (cited at Lewis & Short, pepo).

Other words

  • cēpa, cēpae f. — onion

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. caepa: “also cēpa”; Andresian p. 8; Traupman 72

    The same word, in the spelling with ē for ae; the neuter caepe (cēpe) is as common.

Examples

  • Baba in hortō phasēlōs, caepās, cucumerēs colit.

    Baba grows beans, onions and cucumbers in the garden (after Ep. VII).composed

See also leek, garlic.
